document.title: Afghanistan: Straight Talk with [Excised]
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Taliban File Update
document.note: [Confidential] Ambassador Thomas Simons meets a source who appears to be Shamshad Ahmad, Pakistani envoy to the UN, to discuss Pakistani policy toward the Taliban. Ahmad is pleased at the replacement of UNSMA head Norbert Holl and says Pakistan wants to promote inter-Afghan dialogue. Simons warns that any appearance of preference for replacement Lakdar Brahimi will fuel rumors that Pakistan is pro-Taliban.

events.description: US Ambassador Simons meets Pakistani foreign ministry official at the ministry, discussing shuttle diplomacy, Brahimi, Holl, and Taliban recognition.
Pakistan recognizes the Taliban as Afghanistan's government.
Pakistani Interior Minister Babar's efforts/results in October 1996 on which Holl built.
Urgent call offering the Ambassador a briefing; DCM to follow up.
Ambassador Simons was briefed by a senior Pakistani Foreign Ministry official (apparently Shamshad Ahmad) on the GOP's shuttle diplomacy in Afghanistan and discussed UN envoys Holl and Brahimi.
Embassy Islamabad cabled State the report of the meeting on Pakistan's shuttle diplomacy and the UN's role (cable sent 121215Z Aug 97).
Then-Interior Minister Babar produced results in October 1996 that Holl later built on to counter perceptions that the UN effort was anti-Taliban.
UN Secretary-General's representative Lakhdar Brahimi planned an upcoming visit to the region on Afghanistan.
Riaz Khokhar briefed Under Secretary Pickering in Washington on Pakistan's shuttle diplomacy.
Joint demarches on counterterrorism conventions and the Kashmir hostage crisis were delivered before the discussion on Afghanistan.
Interior Minister Babar's October 1996 initiative, on whose results UN envoy Holl built.
Pakistan recognized the Taliban as Afghanistan's government, after the fall of Mazar-i-Sharif.
US Ambassador Simons met a Pakistani official (likely Shamshad Ahmad) discussing the UN role, Holl, recognition of Taliban, wheat/fuel and Masood.

relationships.detail: Pakistan recognized the Taliban as Afghanistan's government in May 1997.
relationships.quote: PAKISTAN'S SNAP DECISION TO RECOGNIZE TALIBAN AS AFGHANISTAN'S GOVERNMENT IN MAY

relationships.detail: Ambassador stayed behind after demarches for talks on Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: ASKED THE AMBASSADOR TO STAY BEHIND TO DISCUSS OTHER ISSUES

relationships.detail: Holl heads the UN Special Mission on Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: CURRENT UNSMA HEAD NORBERT HOLL

relationships.detail: Brahimi's visit may signal change in UN mission leadership; Pakistan eager to be rid of Holl.
relationships.quote: WHETHER HE CAN CONTAIN GOP ZEAL TO BE RID OF HOLL

relationships.detail: Massoud described as Jamiat-i-Islami commander.
relationships.quote: JAMIAT-I-ISLAMI COMMANDER MASOOD

relationships.detail: Pakistani official asked whether US had contact with Massoud, suggesting the US avoid it.
relationships.quote: ASKED WHETHER THE U.S. HAS HAD CONTACT WITH JAMIAT-I-ISLAMI COMMANDER MASOOD

relationships.detail: Simons is the U.S. Ambassador who classified and authored the cable from Embassy Islamabad.
relationships.quote: CLASSIFIED BY AMBASSADOR THOMAS W. SIMONS, JR.

relationships.detail: The excised interlocutor, apparently Shamshad Ahmad, briefed the Ambassador on the GOP's shuttle diplomacy; his identity is partly inferred from the entity list and the header.
relationships.quote: BRIEFED HIM ON THE GOP'S ONGOING SHUTTLE DIPLOMACY IN AFGHANISTAN

relationships.detail: The GOP is conducting shuttle diplomacy in Afghanistan to promote intra-Afghan dialogue.
relationships.quote: PAKISTAN'S OBJECTIVE IS TO "PROMOTE INTRA-AFGHAN DIALOGUE."

relationships.detail: Pakistan says it wants to help the UN effort, and that any intra-Afghan dialogue would be under UN auspices.
relationships.quote: ANY INTRA-AFGHAN DIALOGUE WOULD BE UNDER UN AUSPICES

relationships.detail: Holl is the current head of the UN Special Mission to Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: CURRENT UNSMA HEAD NORBERT HOLL "HAS NOT BEEN VERY HELPFUL."

relationships.detail: UNSMA is the UN mission on Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: LEADERSHIP OF THE UN MISSION ON AFGHANISTAN

relationships.detail: Brahimi is the UN Secretary-General's representative being sent to the region on Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: UPCOMING VISIT TO THE REGION BY UNSYG REPRESENTATIVE LAKHDAR BRAHIMI

relationships.detail: Pakistan is glad Brahimi is coming as someone else to work on Afghanistan, and Pakistani zeal to be rid of Holl is noted; Brahimi's arrival may signal a change in UN mission leadership.
relationships.quote: GLAD" THAT THE SECRETARY GENERAL IS SENDING SOMEONE ELSE TO WORK WITH THE AFGHANISTAN PROBLEM

relationships.detail: Pakistan is critical of Holl and the Embassy notes GOP zeal to be rid of him; Pakistan denies regarding him as anti-Taliban.
relationships.quote: WHETHER GOP ZEAL TO BE RID OF HOLL IS IN FACT CONTAINABLE

relationships.detail: The GOP will extend utmost cooperation to Brahimi.
relationships.quote: THE GOP WOULD EXTEND "UTMOST COOPERATION" TO BRAHIMI.

relationships.detail: Others perceive Pakistan as supporting the Taliban, a perception the Ambassador contrasts with the UN's perceived anti-Taliban stance.
relationships.quote: PAKISTAN, THE AMBASSADOR CONTINUED, SUFFERED FROM THE OPPOSITE PERCEPTION BY OTHERS: THAT IT SUPPORTED THE TALIBAN.

relationships.detail: Afghans perceived the UN effort under Holl's predecessor and Holl as anti-Taliban.
relationships.quote: A PERCEPTION AMONG AFGHANS THAT THE UN EFFORT WAS ANTI-TALIBAN

relationships.detail: Holl is perceived as anti-Taliban; Pakistan says it never regarded him as such, only insufficiently active.
relationships.quote: THE GOP NEVER REGARDED HOLL AS ANTI-TALIBAN

relationships.detail: Holl worked to counter the anti-Taliban perception by building on the results of Babar's efforts in October 1996.
relationships.quote: BY BUILDING ON THE RESULTS OF THEN PAKISTANI INTERIOR MINISTER NASEERULLAH KHAN BABAR IN OCTOBER 1996

relationships.detail: Babar was then Pakistan's Interior Minister.
relationships.quote: THEN PAKISTANI INTERIOR MINISTER NASEERULLAH KHAN BABAR

relationships.detail: Pakistani Ambassador to Washington Khokhar was briefing Under Secretary Pickering on the shuttle diplomacy.
relationships.quote: PAKISTANI AMBASSADOR TO WASHINGTON RIAZ KHOKHAR WAS BRIEFING U/S PICKERING

relationships.detail: Khokhar is Pakistan's ambassador to Washington.
relationships.quote: PAKISTANI AMBASSADOR TO WASHINGTON RIAZ KHOKHAR

relationships.detail: Pickering is Under Secretary at the State Department.
relationships.quote: BRIEFING U/S PICKERING

relationships.detail: Inderfurth is an Assistant Secretary who will be briefed when he visits Pakistan.

relationships.quote: A/S INDERFURTH WOULD BE BRIEFED WHEN HE VISITS PAKISTAN

relationships.quote: FM AMEMBASSY ISLAMABAD

relationships.quote: WOULD ALSO KEEP THE EMBASSY BRIEFED.

relationships.detail: The Ambassador defended Holl as having been quite active but constrained by factions preferring battlefield solutions.
relationships.quote: THE AMBASSADOR REJOINED THAT HOLL HAS BEEN QUITE ACTIVE

relationships.detail: Pakistan recognized the Taliban as Afghanistan's government in May 1997.
relationships.quote: PAKISTAN'S SNAP DECISION TO RECOGNIZE TALIBAN AS AFGHANISTAN' S GOVERNMENT IN MAY

relationships.detail: Taliban captured Kabul (earlier).
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN'S CAPTURE OF KABUL

relationships.quote: AFTER THE FALL OF MAZAR-I-SHARIF

relationships.detail: Masood described as a Jamiat-i-Islami commander.
relationships.quote: JAMIAT-I-ISLAMI COMMANDER MASOOD

relationships.detail: Shamshad (the Pakistani interlocutor) met the Ambassador and asked about US contact with Masood.
relationships.quote: ASKED WHETHER THE U.S. HAS HAD CONTACT WITH JAMIAT-I-ISLAMI COMMANDER MASOOD

relationships.detail: US has not recently met Masood but keeps contact open with all factions and may meet him.
relationships.quote: WE HAD NOT RECENTLY MET HIM, BUT OUR POLICY IS TO KEEP CONTACT OPEN WITH ALL FACTIONS

relationships.detail: Pakistan regulating wheat and oil flow into Afghanistan to gain leverage over the Taliban.
relationships.quote: CONTROLLING TRADE OF THESE VITAL COMMODITIES MAY GIVE PAKISTAN GREATER LEVERAGE OVER THE TALIBAN

relationships.detail: Brahimi is the incoming UN envoy replacing Holl; Pakistan welcomed Brahimi.
relationships.quote: NOT GOING OVERBOARD IN PAKISTAN'S WELCOME OF BRAHIMI

key_claims: Pakistan describes its shuttle diplomacy as promoting intra-Afghan dialogue under UN auspices.
The US Ambassador warned Pakistan not to hand the US or UN a fait accompli or imply the US would be guarantor.
Pakistan is eager to see UN envoy Norbert Holl replaced by Brahimi, viewing Holl as unhelpful.
Pakistan's May 1997 recognition of the Taliban undermined US efforts to deny responsibility for the Taliban.
Pakistan intends to use control of wheat and fuel flows into Afghanistan as leverage over the Taliban.
A Pakistani official hinted the US should avoid contact with Jamiat commander Massoud.
